Blood and urine cultures should be considered to exclude bacterial causes of reactive polyarthropathy in cases where no obvious infectious or inflammatory focus is identified. Positive blood cultures may be indicative of primary septic polyarthritis of hematogenous origin given relatively low sensitivity of bacterial culture of synovial fluid.

Appendicular radiographs including affected joints are necessary to exclude erosive causes of polyarthropathy, though these diseases are uncommon in dogs and may not be radiographically visible initially.
